2.text: scratch at the skin, and make it full of holes. Be your anger as great as

3.text: is mine! Destroy him speedily, before the coming of the fall!” Indeed, in

4.text: a few days he is dead.¹
4.note: footnote reference marker: mz draft read this as a closing bracket ']'; printed superscript ¹ per U+00B9, pairs with the opener on line 37.

5.text: Told by a Reindeer Chukchee of the Kolyma Country.

7.text: (a) If I want to have any woman, I follow her all the time. When she

8.text: urinates, I see her urine falling down, and then I say, “This is not urine

9.text: that falls down; this is your heart and liver and kidneys, that fall down

10.text: together.” I go to the Morning-Dawn, and I ask him to give me boots with

11.text: iron ice-creepers. With these boots I trample on that woman’s heart and

12.text: intestines, and hurt them with the iron ice-creepers. Then she will have a

13.text: liking for me, and her heart will be hurt with it.

14.text: Told by Hɪyewteˊhɪn at Mariinsky Post, 1900.
14.resolved: Hɪyewteˊhɪn: ɪ = U+026A (twice, in 'Hɪ-' and '-hɪn', both dotless bare stems, contrasted against dotted 'i' in 'liking'/'Post' on neighbouring lines); ˊ = U+02CA stress mark after 'Hiyewte'. mz draft read this as plain ASCII 'Hiyewte hin' with a space for the raised mark.
14.note: Tier-1 personal name; mz draft read plain ASCII 'Hiyewte hin' with a space for the raised mark. See resolved field for codepoint breakdown.

15.text: (b) If I want to have this woman, I take out her heart and liver, then

16.text: I go towards the Evening “direction,” and hang her organs on both sides of

17.text: the Evening. Then I say, “Here is the heart and the liver of that woman.

18.text: Make them entangled in a seal-net! Let her be without her intestines! let

19.text: her pine away with desire for me! — This man is not your husband. This

20.text: is a seal’s carcass drifted to the seashore, rotting upon the pebbles. Every

21.text: wind blows upon it, and its bones are bared. And you are not a woman;

22.text: you are a young reindeer-doe. The smell of the carrion comes to you, and

23.text: you flee away, and come into my possession.”

24.text: Told by Keˊᵋulin (man) in the village of Čeˊčin, 1900.
24.resolved: Keˊᵋulin: ˊ = U+02CA stress after 'Ke'; ᵋ = U+1D4B laryngeal, immediately after the stress mark, before 'ulin' — same Ke'-initial name attested as Keˊᵋulin on 2-229 ('Told by Keˊᵋulin (man) in the village of Mɪˊs˙qᴀn, 1900.'), same formulaic line, only one ground-truth page so below the two-page handle floor, keyed by hand rather than as a lexicon handle. Village name handle {C^e'c^in} -> Čeˊčin (č = c+U+030C) is ratified on 12 other pages via lexicon lookup.
24.as_typed: Told by Keˊᵋulin (man) in the village of {C^e'c^in}, 1900.
24.note: Tier-1 personal name plus toponym; mz draft read 'Keffulin' and 'Cefćin'. See resolved field for codepoint breakdown and the lexicon handle used for the village name.

25.text: 12. INCANTATION USED BY A JEALOUS WOMAN AGAINST HER RIVAL.

26.text: “Then you are this woman! You have so much of my husband’s love

27.text: that he begins to lose all liking for me. But you are not a human being!

28.text: I make you into carrion lying on the pebbly shore, — old carrion inflated
28.note: mz draft read 'Iying' (capital I) for printed 'lying' — confirmed at 2x, ordinary lowercase l.

29.text: with rottenness. I make my husband into a big bear. The bear comes from

30.text: a distant land. He is very hungry; he has been starving for a long time.

31.text: He sees the carrion; seeing it, he eats of it. After a while he vomits it

32.text: out. I make you into the stuff vomited. My husband sees you, and says,

33.text: ‘I do not want it!’ My husband takes to despising you.”
33.note: nested quotation: printed as single curly quotes (U+2018/U+2019) around the husband's exclamation, inside the outer double-quoted speech opened on line 26 and closed here; mz draft had both as straight double quotes.

34.text: At the same time I make this body of mine into a young beaver that

35.text: has just shed his hair. I make smooth every hair of mine. My husband

36.text: will leave his former liking, and turn again to me, because she is repugnant

37.text: ¹ See Bogoras, Chukchee Materials, p. 142.
